text:
clara: FYI discovered a nasty handoff case with background workers and key rotation. We run `rw-worker` as a systemd service that streams logs; when I swap the token file atomically, the worker keeps the old key for minutes and then dies with 403.

hiro: ouch. does the worker spawn child processes that inherit env?

clara: yes it's a long-lived single process that opens persistent HTTP streams. Our current SDK reads env/token files at init only.

omar: two solutions: (A) SDK watches token file changes via inotify (or polling on mac) and rotates in process; (B) document that services must restart on rotation and provide a `rw auth reload` systemd-friendly signal to orchestrate a graceful restart.

clara: we tried a simple polling watch in a dev build and it solved it. downside: extra syscalls and complexity in low-level SDKs.

hiro: what about hybrid: SDK lazy-reads per request but for streams do a single in-stream refresh when 401/403 seen. That avoids file watchers entirely.

omar: good call. Proposed policy: 1) precedence doc: REDWOOD_API_KEY env > REDWOOD_TOKEN_FILE (path) > ~/.config/redwood/token. 2) SDKs: lazy-read with a short TTL (3s) for regular requests. 3) For long-lived streams: on 401/403, attempt: re-read token sources once, replay/resume current in-flight segment, then fatal if still rejected. 4) Optionally support file-watch via config for infra with many restarts.

clara: also request: server could set `X-Reauth-Required: 1` or `Retry-After: 2` on forced revocations so clients can decide immediate behavior instead of guessing.

ci-bot: created issue RBW-3580 (labels: devex, sdk, bg-workers).

hiro: I'll draft a small compatibility matrix for SDKs and add a sample systemd unit snippet to onboarding: show `ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID` + `rw auth reload` example.

omar: I'll PR the SDK change (node + python) to lazy_ttl=3s + stream-refresh-on-401 and tests that simulate atomic token swap. Mention backwards-compatible change in changelog.

clara: thanks! also adding a short note to the sampleapp README: "For services, prefer atomic file swap + `rw auth reload` or enable SDK file-watch option."

ci-bot: linked PRs: #4127 (node sdk), #4128 (python sdk), referenced in RBW-3580.

clara: great. small win for onboarding infra teams.
